title: Telling what already happened
title_target: ເລົ່າເລື່ອງທີ່ຜ່ານມາ — Lào lʉ̂ang thìi phàan maa
goal: Talk about yesterday and last week: what you did, what you have experienced, and what you haven't gotten around to yet — without a single change in verb form.
bekal: ແລ້ວ for things that are done
ເຄີຍ and ບໍ່ເຄີຍ for experiences
ຍັງບໍ່ທັນ for things not done yet
ຕອນ and ຕອນທີ່ for "at that time"

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — Monday morning, weekend stories
dialogs.intro: Budi has just come back from Luang Prabang. Notice that not one verb in this dialog changes form — the past is marked only by time words and the word *ແລ້ວ*.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ທ້າຍ|Thâai][ອາທິດ|aa-thit][ໄປ|pai][ໃສ|sǎi][ມາ|maa]
lines.id: Where did you go this weekend?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ໄປ|Pai][ຫຼວງພະບາງ|Lǔang-Pha-Baang][ມາ|maa] [ໄປ|Pai][ກັບ|kap][ໝູ່|mùu][ສອງ|sǎwng][ຄົນ|khón]
lines.id: Luang Prabang. I went with two friends.
lines.literal: go — Luang-Prabang — come. go — with — friend — two — person.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໂອ້|Ôo] [ມ່ວນ|mùan][ບໍ່|bàw] [ເຈົ້າ|Jâo][ເຄີຍ|khóei][ໄປ|pai][ບໍ່|bàw][ກ່ອນ|kàwn][ໜ້າ|nâa][ນີ້|nîi]
lines.id: Oh, was it fun? Had you been there before?
lines.literal: oh — fun — (question)? you — ever — go — (question) — before — front — this?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່ເຄີຍ|Bàw khóei] [ເທື່ອ|Thʉ̀a][ນີ້|nîi][ເປັນ|pen][ເທື່ອ|thʉ̀a][ທຳອິດ|tham-ít] [ມ່ວນ|Mùan][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai]
lines.id: Never. This was my first time. It was so much fun.
lines.literal: not — ever. time — this — be — time — first. fun — much.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄປ|Pai][ແນວ|neeo][ໃດ|dai] [ຂຶ້ນ|Khʉ̂n][ຍົນ|nyón][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: How did you get there? Did you fly?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່|Bàw] [ຂຶ້ນ|Khʉ̂n][ລົດໄຟ|lot-fái][ໄປ|pai] [ໃຊ້|Sâi][ເວລາ|wée-láa][ສອງ|sǎwng][ຊົ່ວໂມງ|sùa-móong][ເທົ່າ|thao][ນັ້ນ|nân] [ໄວ|Vái][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai]
lines.id: No. I took the train. It only took two hours. Really fast.
lines.literal: no. board — train — go. use — time — two — hour — only — that. fast — much.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄປ|Pai][ເບິ່ງ|bòeng][ຫຍັງ|nyǎng][ແດ່|dèe]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຕອນ|Tawn][ເຊົ້າ|sâo][ໄປ|pai][ເບິ່ງ|bòeng][ຕັກ|ták][ບາດ|bàat] [ແລ້ວ|Lèeo][ກໍ|kaw][ຂຶ້ນ|khʉ̂n][ພູສີ|Phúu-Sǐi] [ຕອນ|Tawn][ບ່າຍ|bàai][ໄປ|pai][ນ້ຳຕົກ|nâm-tók]
lines.id: In the morning I watched the alms giving, then climbed Phousi. In the afternoon I went to the waterfall.
lines.literal: time — morning — go — see — scoop — bowl. then — also — climb — Phousi. time — afternoon — go — water-fall.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi][ກິນ|kin][ອາຫານ|aa-hǎan][ພື້ນເມືອງ|phʉ̂n-mʉang][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Did you get to eat the local food?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi] [ກິນ|Kin][ໄຄ|khái][ແມ່ນ້ຳຂອງ|mèe-nâm-Khǒong][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ແຊບ|Sèep][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ຍັງ|nyáng][ບໍ່|bàw][ທັນ|than][ໄດ້|dâi][ຊື້|sʉ̂ʉ][ຂອງຝາກ|khǎwng-fàak]
lines.id: Yes. I had Mekong river weed — delicious. But I didn't get around to buying souvenirs.
lines.literal: get. eat — river-weed — river-Khong — already. tasty — much. but — still — not — in-time — get — buy — souvenir.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່ເປັນຫຍັງ|Bàw pen nyǎng] [ເທື່ອ|Thʉ̀a][ໜ້າ|nâa][ຂ້ອຍ|khàwy][ຊິ|si][ໄປ|pai][ນຳ|nám]
lines.id: No problem. Next time I'll come along.
lines.literal: not — be — what. time — next — I — will — go — along.

notes: **Lao has NO past tense. Period.** The verb is exactly the same for yesterday, today, and tomorrow. Time is marked by just three things: time words (*ມື້ວານນີ້*), the word *ແລ້ວ lèeo* (already), and context. This is Lao's best news for beginners.

**ແລ້ວ lèeo at the end = "already, done".** *ກິນແລ້ວ* (have eaten), *ໄປແລ້ວ* (has gone). It isn't a past marker but a **completion** marker — which is why it can also be used for the future: *ດຽວຝົນຊິຕົກແລ້ວ* (it's about to start raining).

**ເຄີຍ khóei = "ever, have done before", placed IN FRONT of the verb.** *ຂ້ອຍເຄີຍໄປ* (I've been), *ບໍ່ເຄີຍໄປ* (have never been). ⚠️ Don't mix it up with *ແລ້ວ*: *ໄປແລ້ວ* means "has gone (just now)", *ເຄີຍໄປ* means "has been (at some point in life)".

**ຍັງບໍ່ທັນ nyáng bàw than = "haven't gotten around to it yet".** The word *ທັນ than* means "in time, have the chance". *ຍັງບໍ່ທັນກິນ* (haven't eaten yet), *ບໍ່ທັນລົດ* (missed the bus). In fast conversation, just *ຍັງ* is enough.
**ໄປ…ມາ pai… maa is the typical pattern for "been to… and back".** *ໄປຕະຫຼາດມາ* (been to the market), *ໄປໃສມາ* (where have you been?). The *ມາ maa* at the end says the trip is over and you're back.

**ໄດ້ dâi before a verb means "got to, actually did".** *ໄດ້ກິນ* (got to eat), *ບໍ່ໄດ້ໄປ* (didn't end up going). ⚠️ This differs from *ໄດ້* after a verb, which means "can": *ໄປໄດ້* (can go) versus *ໄດ້ໄປ* (got to go).
**ຕອນ tawn = "time, when", and it opens a time clause.** *ຕອນເຊົ້າ* (in the morning), *ຕອນທີ່ຂ້ອຍໄປ* (when I went), *ຕອນນັ້ນ* (at that time). It's the most common link word in storytelling.

**ແດ່ dèe after a question word asks for a list.** *ໄປເບິ່ງຫຍັງແດ່* (what all did you see?), *ມີໃຜແດ່* (who all was there?), *ໄປໃສແດ່* (where all did you go?). Without *ແດ່*, the question asks about one thing only.

**About ຕັກບາດ ták bàat** — the line of monks receiving alms at dawn in Luang Prabang. If you join in giving, kneel, don't take close-up photos, and cover your shoulders. It's a daily ritual for local people, not a tourist show, and Lao people notice who treats it with respect.

after: **ຫາກໍ *hàa kaw*** and **ເມື່ອກີ້ *mʉ̂a kîi*** both mean "just", but they sit in different places: *ຫາກໍ* goes before the verb (*ຫາກໍມາ* — just arrived), while *ເມື່ອກີ້* stands alone as a time marker (*ເມື່ອກີ້ລາວມາ* — he came a moment ago).

blocks.text: With these ten words you can already tell a long story. Try it now: link five events from your weekend using *ກ່ອນອື່ນ — ແລ້ວກໍ — ຫຼັງຈາກນັ້ນ — ແຕ່ວ່າ — ໃນທີ່ສຸດ*, and read it out loud. It's the single most useful exercise in this whole book.

blocks.text: **ຫຼວງພະບາງ *Lǔang-Pha-Baang*** is the former royal capital and the only Lao town on UNESCO's World Heritage list. Since the Vientiane–Boten high-speed railway opened, a trip that used to take ten winding hours through the mountains now takes two — and it has completely changed how Vientiane people spend their weekends.
**ໄຄ *khái*** (dried, fried river weed) is a Luang Prabang snack with no real equivalent in the West. If someone offers you something that looks like green paper dotted with sesame seeds — try it.

Where did you go this weekend?
Luang Prabang. I went with two friends.
Had you been there before?
Never. This was my first time.
In the morning I watched the alms giving, then climbed Phousi.
I ate the local food, but I didn't get around to buying souvenirs.

ມື້ວານນີ້ຂ້ອຍໄປຕະຫຼາດ — ອາທິດແລ້ວຂ້ອຍພົບບຸນມີ — ຄືນນີ້ຝົນຕົກ — ຕອນເຊົ້ານີ້ຂ້ອຍກິນເຝີ — ເມື່ອກີ້ລາວມາ
ທ້າຍອາທິດໄປໃສມາ — ເຈົ້າເຄີຍໄປບໍ່ — ເທື່ອນີ້ເປັນເທື່ອທຳອິດ — ໄປເບິ່ງຫຍັງແດ່ — ຍັງບໍ່ທັນຊື້ຂອງຝາກ
ທ້າຍອາທິດໄປໃສມາ — ໄປຫຼວງພະບາງມາ ໄປກັບໝູ່ສອງຄົນ — ເຈົ້າເຄີຍໄປບໍ່ກ່ອນໜ້ານີ້ — ບໍ່ເຄີຍ ເທື່ອນີ້ເປັນເທື່ອທຳອິດ — ຕອນເຊົ້າໄປເບິ່ງຕັກບາດ ແລ້ວກໍຂຶ້ນພູສີ — ກິນອາຫານພື້ນເມືອງແລ້ວ ແຕ່ຍັງບໍ່ທັນຊື້ຂອງຝາກ
